notes: SHIP v1.14.426 - A NORMALIZATION UPGRADE MIGRATES STORED DATA. DERIVED CACHES ARE NOT PERMANENT TRUTH (owner ruling 2026-08-09, after a FAILED device verify). WHAT FAILED AND WHY. The phone still showed s4:099 as NO HOST DATA IN MASTER, 68 CABLES against v1.14.425, and the screen said RESTORED FROM CACHE. The served build was proven first and was NOT the problem: version.json, sw.js CACHE_VERSION and the dct-ios.html app stamp all read v1.14.425, and the served bytes contained section 9a, CUTSHEET_ENDPOINT and hostsFromCutsheet. The cause was the DATA. v1.14.424 corrected how components are DERIVED, but derivation only ever ran inside phantom_parseMaster - so it ran at IMPORT and nowhere else. A device that already held a Master restored the inventory built by the OLD normalizer, verbatim, forever. adoptRestored assigns the stored object and normalizes nothing, so correct served code sat in front of data built by code that no longer exists. EXACTLY WHAT WAS BEING RESTORED - the question asked and answered. Not the raw workbook, which is retained NOWHERE. Not a parsed intermediate. PHANTOM_MASTER_STORE persists racksByCab WHOLE, so what comes back is the normalized derived inventory: per-cab hosts arrays, cablesOut and cablesIn, plus siteCode, sourceFile, sourceFileHash, siteVars and the .414 counts. So yes - s4:099's old 0 components + 68 cables was persisted and restored directly. A stale comment at the restore site claimed hosts/cables are not persisted; it had been false for a long time and is corrected in this ship. WHY NO RE-UPLOAD IS NEEDED. The normalizer never needed the workbook. Its only inputs are cable endpoints, and every persisted cable object carries aLoc, aDns, aModel, zLoc, zDns and zModel verbatim. Everything .424 derives at import is therefore re-derivable at boot from what is already on the device. THE FIX, IN FOUR PARTS. 1. MASTER_NORM_VERSION - a normalizer generation stamp, separate from schemaVersion. schemaVersion says whether a payload can be READ; it never said which normalizer BUILT it, and that gap is the whole defect. 1 = SITE-HOSTS only, 2 = dual-source. Absent means 1 by definition. Additive and optional exactly like sourceFile, siteVars and the .414 counts: load() still validates ONLY schemaVersion, so nothing that already restores stops restoring. 2. ONE NORMALIZER, TWO CALLERS. The endpoint loop moved out of phantom_parseMaster into master_normalizeEndpoints and is now PURE - it returns what should be added and mutates nothing. Import and migration run the SAME engine over the same inputs, which is the only reason a rebuilt Master is guaranteed to equal a re-imported one. Purity is load-bearing, not style: the migration must persist before anything goes live, and a normalizer that mutated in place would already have contaminated the live object. 3. BOOT MIGRATION. If a restored payload predates the current generation, its inventory is rebuilt and the upgrade is persisted atomically THROUGH PHANTOM_MASTER.replace - which saves FIRST and goes live SECOND, and DISCARDS a candidate it cannot persist while a good Master is active. Two outcomes only: upgraded in both halves, or untouched in both halves. Structural sharing means only racks that actually gain components are rebuilt. 4. A ROUND-TRIP DATA-LOSS TRAP, FOUND AND FIXED. save() read sourceFileHash and totalCables from .stats, which ONLY a fresh parse has - a restored payload carries them at top level. Re-saving a restored Master through the old code wrote null for both, discarding the Master's identity and cable count as a side effect of fixing its components. save() now reads both shapes. Same whitelist class that ate the enrichment fields. HONEST FAILURE MODES, ALL PROVEN BY TEST: rebuild-failed leaves the stamp alone so a later boot retries; no-cables-retained states that a rebuild is impossible on device rather than reporting a successful no-op, and refuses to stamp itself current so a re-import stays the path; persist-refused leaves BOTH halves untouched. TESTS: new spec 16-normalization-migration.spec.js, seven tests, all green. The fixture runs the production parser over the owner's REAL rows, then strips the endpoint components and the normVersion stamp and writes the payload straight to localStorage - byte-for-byte the shape a pre-.424 device holds, not an approximation. Pinned: a v1 payload restores as 0 components and migrates to 19; the right models at the right RUs, not just the right count; SITE-HOSTS racks are not padded and suppression fires on the migration path; the upgrade is IN STORAGE, not memory-only; the round trip keeps hash and cables; IDEMPOTENT - a second boot finds it current and does not duplicate; a cable-less Master reports that it cannot be rebuilt. The real rows now live in one shared module so specs 15 and 16 can never drift onto different data. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4583/4583, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep. No UI surface changed. No Forge patch. ?legacy=1 unaffected. DEVICE-VERIFY: just open PHANTOM and go to s4:099. It must rebuild to 19 components with NO re-import: nine GPU-B300 at RU 35/32/29/26/23/20/17/14/11, an SN2201 at 46, eight PS-1RU-06 at 42/41/40/39 and 9/8/7/6, a CDU-4RU-03 at 2 - and it must keep its 68 cables. Then fully reload and confirm the same 19 persist. Console line if wanted: window.__phantomNormMigration.
